input:
Once the standby pump is in service and carrying the full flow, the duty pump is stopped from the local panel and left selected to hand, so that it cannot be restarted remotely. The discharge valve of the duty pump is closed first, then its suction valve, letting the motor-driven travel complete on each and then shutting both fully by hand to seat them properly. The section of pipework between the two closed valves, together with the pump casing itself, still holds stored pressure after isolation, and for this reason the drain on the casing is cracked open slowly, into the closed drain system, and left open until the flow from it has stopped. The vent at the high point of the casing is then opened and left open as well; if the casing is still blowing at the vent, it is still pressurised, and under no circumstances should any joint on the casing be touched until the vent has run quiet and the local pressure gauge is reading zero.

The casing is drained down fully, and the isolation is proved at the drain, because a drain that flows again after running dry shows that either the suction valve or the discharge valve is passing, in which case the isolation is made again with the second valve on that line before further work goes ahead. The lock and the tag are fitted to each of the closed valves under the PTW arrangements, and the isolation is entered in the isolation register against the duty pump. As a final proof, a start of the duty pump is attempted from the local panel with the isolation in force, and the pump must not turn at all. With the unit isolated and proved in this condition, the seal replacement itself takes about 45 min to complete. The gland follower is then slackened off evenly, a small amount on each stud in turn, with the drain left open underneath the seal housing, so that any liquid that is still held behind the follower will run away to the drain rather than over the hands of the fitter, and the follower is drawn back along the shaft

With the standby pump running and carrying the full flow, the duty pump is stopped from the local panel and left selected to hand. Close the discharge valve of the duty pump first and then its suction valve, and shut both valves fully by hand after the motor-driven travel stops. The section of pipework between the two closed valves, and the pump casing with it, holds stored pressure after isolation, and the drain on the casing is cracked open slowly, to the closed drain system, until the flow from it stops. The vent at the casing high point is then opened and left open; a casing that still blows at the vent is still pressurised, and no joint on the casing is touched until the vent runs quiet and the local pressure gauge reads zero.

Drain the casing fully and prove the isolation at the drain: a drain that starts to flow again after it has run dry shows a passing suction or discharge valve, and the isolation is made again with the second valve on that line before work continues. Fit the lock and the tag to each closed valve under the PTW, and enter the isolation in the isolation register against the duty pump. Attempt a start of the duty pump from the local panel with the isolation in force; the pump must not turn. With the unit isolated in this state, the seal replacement itself takes about 45 min. The gland follower is then slackened evenly, a little on each stud in turn, while the drain stays open below the seal housing, so that any liquid still held behind the follower runs to the drain and not over the hands of the fitter, and the follower is drawn back along the shaft
